text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-French Defence Minister Millon said his country supports a political solution between Lebanon and Israel.
-The Higher Lebanese Syrian Council will meet in Damascus at the beginning of March.
-Lebanon expressed its reservations on participation in the meetings of the environmental committee of multinationl Middle East peace talks.
-A Beirut magistrate demanded the death penalty for jailed former Christian warlord Samir Geagea on charges of ordering the murder of prime minister Rashid Karami in 1987.
-Chairman of Middle East Airlines Khalid Salam said the company's loss in 1996 was $50 million.
-An unidentified man was blown to pieces when a small bomb exploded in the Palestinian refugee camp of Ain el-Hilweh in south Lebanon.
-Minister of Environment Shhayyeb issued an order barring the import of industrial waste.
-Australia's Prime Minister will visit Beirut in the first half of March to sign a commercial agreement with Lebanon.
-Lebanon filed a complaint against Israel with the five-nation committee monitoring a ceasefire in south Lebanon over an Israeli air raid that wounded a civilian.
